newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends lower after early fund sales.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends lower after early fund sales.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures closed lower after a wave of fund sales earlier on Monday, but losses were limited by trade buying at session lows, traders said.
May ended down 17 stg at 1,002 stg per tonne and July lost 13 to 1,021. Total volume reached 6,388 contracts.
Traders said fund sales emerged from the start to help push July through support at 1,025, 1,014 and 1,000 to hit the lowest level since April 10.
A large European firm sold 100 May and 300 July contracts in the morning, traders said.
But trade buying emerged in the afternoon at the session's lows to lift prices off the floor, traders said.

Despite the day's losses, some analysts said cocoa should continue to trade mostly sideways in the near-term. They said technicals were pointing to neutral ground, with stochastics lingering around 50 percent.

They do not expect any dramatic moves until July either breaks critical support between 987 and the April 9 low of 980 or moves back above resistance near 1,050, a tick above the highs made on April 3 and 4.
If July breaks out in either direction, traders expected funds to jump in and steer the move.

Fundamentally, near record declared arrivals in the Ivory Coast and mid-crop estimates of 160,000 tonnes coupled with trends in European and U.S. grinds data were seen implying that the deficit this year will not be as large as earlier forecasts, broker GNI said.
In options, 70 July 1,100 stg calls, 15 July 1,200 calls and 70 July 1,000 puts changed hands in the afternoon.
